subject: ap_precalc
note: AP CSA is the day after, 2027-05-12. Plan the final week around both.

exam._note: mcq_weight, frq_weight, and unit_weights describe the REAL AP exam's official section and unit weighting, for reference only. The readiness engine does not apply them: composite_pct is a flat percent-correct across all server-graded attempts with no section weighting, and readiness.per_unit_min holds every unit to the same floor regardless of its exam weight.

readiness.frq_calibrated_note: False until the FRQ grader is validated against an officially scored College Board response. While false, the frq criterion is reported as pending rather than failed, and free-response evidence does not count toward readiness.
readiness.reuse_days_note: How long a question stays 'already answered' before it counts as evidence again, read by select.js. Sized to THIS bank, which is tiny: 48 items, while one full sitting needs 42 of them (90% of 46). At ~4 answers a day of ordinary drilling the whole bank is worked through in under a fortnight, and anything above 21 days — window_span_days_max / (consecutive_qualifying_mocks - 1) — would require the three qualifying sittings to be question-disjoint, i.e. 84 distinct items from a bank of 48. So 14. This is a symptom, not a solution: the real fix is more Precalc items (33 exam-tested topics still have none, which the build already reports as an error). Beyond the window select.js still serves the least-recently-seen question rather than refusing, and labels it a repeat.

_documentation_only._note: Keys below are not read anywhere in worker/src. They record intent that was never wired into the readiness engine, or historical context; treat every value here as reference, not as an enforced rule.

reduced_confidence_mocks_min.note: Meant to raise the required mock count when the evidence is weak (e.g. still bank-only). Not implemented — no criterion or advisory reads it.

difficulty_gap_max.note: Meant to cap how far the question bank's difficulty can drift from the official exam's. Not implemented — no criterion or advisory reads it.

units_class_only.note: Unit 4 is class-only (not tested on the exam). This key is decorative: the actual exclusion mechanism is that "4" is simply omitted from the `units` array above, which is what the readiness engine and topic selection both read. Editing this key changes nothing — edit `units` instead.

historical_note: 4-5 rate: ~50% (2024) -> ~54% (2025) -> 58% (2026); 2026 was 5=29%, 4=29%, 3=24%, 2=11%, 1=7%. Floors are an INITIAL setting - revisit after the first three real mocks and raise rather than lower if in doubt. Unit 4 is class-only and excluded from readiness because it is omitted from the `units` array above, not because of the `units_class_only` key (documentation only, see `_documentation_only`).
